A Lagos chain wants graded, washed tomatoes and rodo on every shelf.
Hotels, schools and party caterers need jollof base by the drum.
State distributors take sachet paste and dried tatashe by the truck.
ECOWAS traders load ground pepper sacks for markets along the coast.
Diaspora shops abroad order sealed dried rodo with a taste of home.

milestones.blurb: Ten depots share plastic crates, so far fewer tomatoes get crushed on the road.

milestones.title: Dried Pepper King

milestones.title: Diaspora Kitchens
milestones.blurb: Stores in London and Houston. Jollof abroad now tastes the way it does at home.

milestones.title: World Pepper Icon
milestones.blurb: 500 depots on three continents. From one paint bucket to feeding the world.

research.claim: Post-harvest losses in Nigeria's tomato sector reach as high as 40%, and on the 1,000 km Kaduna to Lagos trip in raffia baskets barely half the produce is said to arrive in good condition, which is why plastic crates are being promoted.
The first refrigerated tomato truck from Kaduna State to Lagos in December 2017 carried 933 crates of 20 kg each and took about two days.
Traders in Kano State sun-dry tomato, pepper and okra to cope with gluts and sell in the off season; dried pepper is the most profitable and is graded A, B or C by colour.
Kano has yearly tomato gluts where surplus rots, only about 20% of Nigeria's vegetables are processed, and the country spent over $350m importing tomato paste in 2025.
